# Security Policy

## Supported versions

RepoCortex is alpha. Only the latest tagged release receives fixes. There is no
backport branch.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Report privately through GitHub's advisory flow:
<https://github.com/satyendrakumarsingh/repocortex/security/advisories/new>

Do not open a public issue for a vulnerability.

Expect an acknowledgement within 3 working days and an assessment within 10.
If a fix is warranted we will agree a disclosure date with you; we default to
publishing the advisory once a fixed release is available.

## What RepoCortex does with your code

RepoCortex reads your repository and writes a SQLite index under `.repocortex/`.
Indexing, resolving and serving make no network request: `repocortex serve`
opens a local, loopback-only HTTP listener for its portal, but nothing in
those code paths makes an outbound call. `repocortex scip import` only reads a
`.scip` file from a local path you give it; it has no remote-fetch mode. The
one command that reaches the network is `repocortex indexers install`, which
shells out to `npm`, `go install`, or `docker pull` to provision a
compiler-backed SCIP indexer you explicitly asked for, pinned by version and
verified by digest before it runs.

Your source never leaves your machine.

## Threat model and hardening

The design-level document — what RepoCortex treats as untrusted input, how
redaction and path containment work, and what an attacker controlling a
repository can and cannot do — is
[docs/security.md](docs/security.md).

## Verifying a release

Every release ships `SHA256SUMS` and an SPDX SBOM, and every archive carries
SLSA build provenance generated by the tagged CI run:

```bash
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
gh attestation verify repocortex_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz \
  --repo github.com/satyendrakumarsingh/repocortex
```

If either check fails, do not run the binary. Report it through the advisory
link above.
